seo.title: ODDfest 2026 — Impact report
seo.description: What ODDfest, ODDference and Creative Week did in 2026, set against 2025: the numbers, the grants, the lineup and partners, press, what people told us, the promises we kept and missed, and what changes for 2027.

title: Against all ODDs. Again.
titlePremise: In 2026 one festival became a week, a conference and a building.

letter.point: Most of it worked anyway, because none of it was ours alone.
letter.body:
We turned one festival into a week. ODDspace opened in Vallila in April. Creative Week began on 8 June at Maria 01, ODDference ran for the first time, over two days, and ODDfest filled the Friday and Saturday from Vanha Ylioppilastalo to Tavastia. On paper that's too much for one small non-profit. Some weeks it was.

Everyone carried a piece of it. Partners opened their own rooms, from Maria 01 to Amos Rex and Taidehalli. 166 artists, performers, speakers and collectives brought their work and their crowds. 125 volunteers kept things calm when they weren't. The City of Helsinki and four foundations backed the year before anyone knew how it would turn out. Count everyone who had a pass, and almost a third of them were there to make it happen, not to watch it.

We also got things wrong. Too much ran at once, and some rooms were too quiet for the work in them. We missed the growth targets we set ourselves a year ago, and not by a little. People told us so, plainly, and they were right. This report puts that next to what went well, because both are true.

So 2027 changes shape. ODDfest becomes Helsinki's creative week of independently made events, and ODDference stays the room where creative expertise meets business.

Thank you, every one of you, from the open call in February to the last night in June. We survived this one together, again, and that's the only reason there's a next one.

direct.title: What happened in the rooms.
direct.body: Three programmes in one week, each with its own job: Creative Week to open the city, ODDference to put creative expertise in front of business, ODDfest to give the work a stage.

items.title: A week, not a weekend
items.body: Creative Week ran from 8 to 14 June with partner-hosted events across Helsinki, from founders and artists in one room at Maria 01 to a futures salon for around 300 guests at Taidehalli.

items.title: Creatives as the experts
items.body: ODDference ran two days: more than 50 speakers, more than 30 sessions. Ten of the fourteen attendees who answered our form gave it 4 or 5 out of 5 for showing what creative expertise is worth to business, work and society.

items.title: On the stages

items.title: Across the city
items.body: Creative Week ran in partners' rooms: Junction at Maria 01, FiBAN's angels at Amos Rex, Hanaholmen and Nordic Culture Point at Oodi, and the Soirée of Serendipity at Taidehalli.

items.title: At the tables
items.body: EMU Growth Partners hosted the networking space and the lunch at ODDference. Nescafé, Mikkeller and Blend Beverages brought the drinks.

items.title: Behind it
items.body: The City of Helsinki and four foundations backed the year. 16bit, Roudaamo, Rajupaja and ODDproduction handled production, and five media partners, from Bonnier News Finland to Radio Helsinki, took it to their audiences.

items.title: Money met culture
items.body: The Creative Capital Gathering put investors, foundations, funds and FiBAN's angels in one room at Amos Rex around one question: what does it really mean to invest in the creative industries? It was built to happen every year.

items.title: Startups met artists
items.body: Creative x Tech, with Junction and Maria 01, brought Helsinki's startup scene and its creative scene into the same evening, where they rarely are.

items.title: A building to come back to
items.body: ODDspace opened in Vallila on 17 April: a workspace, event space and music studio, with public events every week, from ODDrunning.club to Coffee on the House.

items.title: A Nordic conversation
items.body: With Hanaholmen and Nordic Culture Point, a free public panel at Oodi asked, in Swedish, whether culture is decoration, product or part of society's structure.

items.title: Backing that lasts two years
items.body: The Kordelin Foundation's Major Cultural Projects grant runs into 2027, to build new structures between culture and business that outlast a single event.

items.title: Studied by others
items.body: Two Humak cultural-management students studied participation at ODDfest 2026. They found what we found: too many programmes at once, and meeting people is not the same as belonging.

promises.title: What we promised in 2025, checked.
promises.lede: Our 2025 report ended with what 2026 would bring. Here's each promise in that report's own words, and what happened. The ones about shape we mostly kept. The ones about size we didn't.

items.did: ODDference and ODDfest ran 11–13 June, at Bio Rex and on Lasipalatsi Square, and out across the centre to Tavastia, Vanha Ylioppilastalo and Kamppi Chapel.

items.said: Grow to 8,000–10,000 visitors, sell 3,000+ full-access tickets and reach 30% international attendance.
items.did: We didn't get close: about 3,300 visits across the week, and 16% of passes bought in English. The week grew in shape, not in size.

items.said: Build a week-long creative city festival around it: Helsinki Creative Week.
items.did: Creative Week ran 8–14 June, with more than 1,000 people at partner events across Helsinki.

items.said: Double media reach, website traffic and partner engagement.
items.did: LinkedIn followers doubled and impressions grew almost five-fold, mostly through paid posts. The press we can link to fell from 20+ pieces to eight, and partners from 75 to 64.

items.said: Free public installations and activations across Helsinki's central areas.
items.did: Parts of the week were free, like the public panel at Oodi with Hanaholmen and Nordic Culture Point. There was no city-wide programme of installations.

items.said: More extensive open calls for artists and programme and workshop leaders.
items.did: Open calls opened on 26 February. 35 proposals came in to host at Creative Week, 8 were accepted, and 125 people joined as volunteers.

items.said: A sustainability roadmap, waste-reduction targets and a full carbon and waste audit.
items.did: We didn't publish a roadmap, set targets or run the audit in 2026.

items.said: Beyond ODDfest: a professional, conference-style format during the week.
items.did: It became ODDference: two days, 30+ sessions and 50+ speakers, with creative practitioners on stage as the experts.

items.said: The ODDside: year-round events, programmes and spaces, from an accelerator to residencies and masterclasses.
items.did: ODDspace opened in Vallila on 17 April with public events every week. The accelerator, residencies and masterclasses didn't run.

items.title: Too much at once
items.body: Visitors, volunteers and an independent student study said the same thing: too many programmes ran in parallel, and some rooms stayed quiet. "Less would have been more," one attendee wrote.

items.title: Hard to find your way
items.body: Finding your way around scored 2.5 out of 5. The web schedule was hard to use on a phone, signage differed from venue to venue, and the ticket types confused people.

items.title: Volunteers needed more from us
items.body: Volunteers rated onboarding 3.6 out of 5. They asked for one channel instead of many, roles set before the first shift, and somewhere backstage to rest and eat.

items.title: Not enough people knew
items.body: The most common request across all three forms: tell more people, earlier, outside Helsinki and in Finnish as well as English. Several found ODD by accident.

items.title: Reach we paid for isn't reach we earned
items.body: LinkedIn impressions grew almost five-fold, but 86% were paid for. Organic impressions fell by almost a third, and the press we can list fell from 20+ pieces to eight.

next.headline: A different shape for the same argument.
next.body:
ODDfest 2027 is Helsinki's creative week: independently made events across the city, brought together in one shared programme. ODDference 2027 takes place alongside it, where creative and cultural practitioners take the stage as experts.

No dates, venues or programme yet, because none of them are decided. We're collecting event ideas now.
